question.worked_solution:
Let's denote the indefinite integral by $I=\int \frac{{ln}^{3}⁡z}{z}\,\text{d}z.$

To use integration by parts, let's suppose that

$$
\begin{aligned}u={ln}^{3}⁡z\, & ⇒\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}z}=\frac{3{ln}^{2}⁡z}{z}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}z}=\frac{1}{z}\, & ⇒\,v=\int \frac{1}{z}\,\text{d}z=\operatorname{ln}⁡z.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =\int \frac{{ln}^{3}⁡z}{z}\,\text{d}z \\  & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}z}\,\text{d}z \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}z}\,\text{d}z \\  & ={ln}^{3}⁡z(\operatorname{ln}⁡z)-\int (\operatorname{ln}⁡z)(\frac{3{ln}^{2}⁡z}{z})\,\text{d}z \\  & ={ln}^{4}⁡z-3\int \frac{{ln}^{3}⁡z}{z}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={ln}^{4}⁡z-3I.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for $I.$ We can ignore the constant of integration in this case, because it is insignificant for further evaluation of the definite integral.

$$
\begin{aligned}I & ={ln}^{4}⁡z-3I \\ 4I & ={ln}^{4}⁡z \\ I & =\frac{{ln}^{4}⁡z}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate our definite integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{{ln}^{3}⁡z}{z}\,\text{d}z & =\frac{1}{4}({ln}^{4}⁡z){|}_{1}^{e} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}({ln}^{4}⁡(e)-{ln}^{4}⁡(1)) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$
